issues.legal_issue: A direction requiring a transferee to pay land revenue to the State does not, by itself, constitute rent or customary dues payable to the landowner.
material_facts: The deed required the transferees to pay land revenue to the State.
It did not stipulate that the transferees pay rent or customary dues to the landowner, or direct that the revenue be paid out of an amount otherwise due to the landowner.
The annual land revenue was a liability attached to the property and was not deducted from rent or other perquisites payable to the landowner.
issues.conclusion: The requirement to pay land revenue was not a stipulation for rent or michavaram payable to the landowner.
issues.legal_principle: A payment to the State of revenue for the property is not rent to the landowner where it is paid on the transferee’s own behalf and is not deducted from an amount due to the landowner. This accords with section 76(c) of the Transfer of Property Act, under which a mortgagee in possession ordinarily pays public charges from the property’s income absent a contrary contract. The Court applied Patel Bhuder Mayji v. Jat Mamdaji Kalaji, [1969] 3 S.C.R. 690; it distinguished Sankunni Variar v. Neelakandhan Nambudripad, I.L.R. [1944] Mad. 254, where revenue was deducted from rent due to the landlord, and did not follow the reasoning in Parameswaran Embranthiri v. Narasimha Nambudri, [1962] K.L.T. 404, where no rent was fixed or stipulated.

rule.if: kanam_redemption_dispute and revenue_paid_to_state and revenue_not_paid_from_amount_due_to_owner and no_rent_or_customary_dues_stipulated

predicates.kanam_redemption_dispute: The proceeding concerned redemption of a land transaction, with one side claiming it was a mortgage and the other claiming a tenancy.
predicates.revenue_paid_to_state: The transferee was required to pay the property revenue to the State.
predicates.revenue_not_paid_from_amount_due_to_owne: The revenue payment was not directed to be made from rent or another amount payable to the landowner.
predicates.no_rent_or_customary_dues_stipulated: The deed did not stipulate payment of rent or customary dues to the landowner.

issues.definition: When a redemption dispute involves revenue paid to the State rather than from an amount due to the landowner, and no rent or customary dues are stipulated, that revenue payment is not rent to the owner.

issues.legal_issue: Whether a land transaction creates a lease or a mortgage depends on its substance, terms, and surrounding circumstances rather than its description alone.
material_facts: The suit sought redemption of the transaction, while the transferees claimed that the deed created a tenancy and protected them against eviction.
The deed provided no renewal term and no payment of customary dues or rent to the landowner.
The transferees were to enjoy the property in lieu of interest on their advance after paying land revenue to the State.
The deed provided for surrender of the property by registered release on repayment and for return of the counterpart and prior documents.
The advance bore a substantial proportion to the value of the property.
A counterpart of the deed had been executed.
issues.conclusion: The transaction was a mortgage, not a lease, and the landowner’s successors were entitled to redeem it; the appeal was dismissed.
issues.legal_principle: The description of an instrument is not decisive; its terms, the parties’ intention, surrounding circumstances, and conduct must be considered. A lease is indicated by an intention that the transferee enjoy the property in lieu of rent or perquisites, provisions for renewal, or customary dues. A mortgage is indicated by a substantial advance relative to the property’s value and by enjoyment in lieu of interest, repayment-linked surrender, and return of documents; the absence of a repayment-by-sale provision does not rule out a mortgage, and a counterpart is not conclusive. Under section 2(22) of the Kerala Land Reforms Act, 1964, the definition of kanam includes the specified incidents of customary dues or renewal. The Court relied on Cherumanalil Lakshmi v. Mulivil Kunninamkandy Narayani, [1967] 1 S.C.R. 314; Kunhiparan v. V. Naicken, [1967] K.L.T. 646; Kunhirama Nambiar v. Pairu Kurup, [1969] K.L.T. 62; Hussain Thangal v. Ali, [1961] K.L.T. 1033; and Patel Bhuder Mayji v. Jat Mamdaji Kalaji, [1969] 3 S.C.R. 690, and considered the contrasting reasoning in Parameswaran Embranthiri v. Narasimha Nambudri, [1962] K.L.T. 404, and Sankunni Variar v. Neelakandhan Nambudripad, I.L.R. [1944] Mad. 254.

rule.if: mortgage_redemption_dispute and substantial_advance_to_property_value and enjoyment_in_lieu_of_interest and repayment_requires_surrender_and_document_return and no_rent_or_customary_dues_to_owner and no_renewal_term

predicates.mortgage_redemption_dispute: The proceeding sought redemption of a transaction alleged to be a mortgage, while the transferee claimed protection as a tenant.
predicates.substantial_advance_to_property_value: The amount advanced was a substantial proportion of the value of the property.
predicates.enjoyment_in_lieu_of_interest: The transferee was to enjoy the property’s benefits in lieu of interest on the advance.
predicates.repayment_requires_surrender_and_documen: The deed provided for surrender of the property and return of related documents upon repayment.
predicates.no_rent_or_customary_dues_to_owner: The deed did not provide for rent or customary dues payable to the landowner.
predicates.no_renewal_term: The deed contained no provision for renewal of the transferee’s enjoyment.

issues.definition: When a redemption dispute involves a substantial advance, enjoyment in lieu of interest, repayment-linked surrender and document return, no rent or customary dues to the owner, and no renewal term, the transaction is a mortgage rather than a lease.
